Apple just released the iOS 26.6 RC version along with its companion updates. Apple's official release notes confirm a new feature has been added to prepare users' iPhones for iOS 27.

Apple will begin Spotlight indexing work starting with iOS 26.6, getting iPhones ready for iOS 27

It is uncommon for Apple to explicitly mention future software updates in the release notes of a new version.

However, this has indeed happened today with the release of iOS 26.6 RC.

Below are the official release notes for iOS 26.6:

iOS 26.6 is primarily a bug fix and security update, as the beta versions revealed virtually no new features.

Nevertheless, the mention of Spotlight indexing work is worth noting.

When the iOS 27 beta was first released last month, developers found that iPhones spent a long time performing indexing work, with the process often lasting a week or even longer in many cases.

It turns out Apple does not want users to experience the same situation again when iOS 27 is publicly released this fall.

Instead, Apple is completing most of the indexing work in advance through iOS 26.6, thereby providing a smoother experience for iOS 27.

Therefore, if you notice your iPhone performing Spotlight indexing after installing iOS 26.6, this is expected, as the new Siri and Spotlight overhaul in iOS 27 will benefit from this preparatory work.
